notes: distinct_drugs_with_text counts distinct DrugBank entries used (51). distinct_book_names_with_text counts book spellings as the coordinator did (46 listed names + 7 aliases + AMD3100 + AMP = 55; Baclofen/baclofen, Caffeine/caffeine, Disulfiram/disulfiram, Ethanol/Alcohol and glutamate/L-glutamic acid map to one or two entries each).

Rule applied for 'disagrees': DrugBank gives the opposite direction on the same target (Baclofen, Topiramate GABA-A), or states a different target and never mentions the book's target. Records of the second kind where the book's target is simply absent from DrugBank's text are marked kind 'different target, book target not mentioned' in the disagreements list so they can be filtered. The coordinator's four known disagreements are all confirmed from the text; Riluzole is the weakest (DrugBank mentions glutamate release and 'excitatory amino acid receptors' but not receptor antagonism).

Apadenoson entry: the text under this entry names BMS068645 and ATL146e, not apadenoson. R-130964 entry: the text under this entry describes clopidogrel and its active metabolite. Both were used because the file names the entry as the book drug; the identity link comes from the file, not from the text.
DPMA and MCCG: per coordinator instruction, not matched to any entry by name; marked cannot compare, identity unconfirmed.

AMP: raw PubChem file 6083 text (SourceName DrugBank, DB00131 'Adenosine phosphate') is identical to the 'Adenosine phosphate' entry in drugbank_moa_text.json. AMD3100: raw PubChem file 65015 (DrugBank DB06809 'Plerixafor').
Bash was refused in this session, so counts were made by hand from the Grep/Read output; they were cross-checked by chapter (268 = sum of per-chapter counts).
